title: Spring AOP versus AspectJ
context: What is the difference between Spring AOP and AspectJ?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Spring knowledge and questions
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: Spring AOP is proxy-based. It works only on Spring beans and only for method calls through the proxy, and it needs no special compiler. AspectJ weaves aspects into the bytecode, at compile time, load time or with an agent. It works on any object and any join point, including field access and constructors, and has no self-invocation problem. Spring AOP is enough for most application code. Choose AspectJ for full join point coverage.

points.title: Proxy versus weaving
points.why: Spring AOP uses runtime proxies. AspectJ modifies the bytecode.

points.title: Coverage
points.why: AspectJ supports field access and constructors. Spring AOP supports only method calls on beans.
